questions.question: When you tailgate (drive too close to another car's rear bumper):

options.text: You can make other drivers angry and frustrated.
You cannot get a traffic ticket.
You help reduce traffic jams.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can make other drivers angry and frustrated.
questions.explanation: Most rear-end crashes happen because of tailgating. To avoid tailgating, use the Three Second Rule. When the car ahead passes a point like a sign, count one-thousand-one, one-thousand-two, one-thousand-three. If you reach that point before you finish counting, you are too close.

questions.question: If a traffic light is green but a police officer signals you to stop, you should:

options.text: Obey the officer.
Obey the traffic light.
Do what the car in front of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey the officer.
questions.explanation: Always obey a police officer's instructions, even if they go against traffic laws, signs, signals, or road markings.

questions.question: If you are in a traffic crash, you must file a written report with the DMV:

options.text: Only if you or the other driver is injured.
If there is more than $1,000 in property damage or any injuries.
Only if you caused the crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: If there is more than $1,000 in property damage or any injuries.
questions.explanation: You must file a DMV report within 10 days if a crash causes death, any injury, or more than $1,000 in property damage. Your insurance agent, broker, or lawyer can file the report for you in some cases.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road surface. To prevent it in rain, you should:

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: In rain, slow down to reduce the risk of hydroplaning. Driving too fast can make your tires lose contact with the road, making your car hard to control.

questions.question: You are turning left at a corner. You should yield the right-of-way to:

options.text: Cars coming toward you that are also turning left.
All cars coming toward you.
Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for the walk signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: All cars coming toward you.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and cars moving on their green light.

questions.question: The correct way to make a right turn is to:

options.text: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the center before turning.
Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
Approach from the right lane, then move toward the middle of the street before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
questions.explanation: Before turning right, signal to warn other drivers. Slow down and stay as close as possible to the right curb as you approach the intersection.

questions.question: A broken yellow center line means:

options.text: You cannot pass.
You can pass on the right when the road ahead is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can cross it to pass on the left if the road ahead is clear.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, you can proceed in the arrow's direction if:

options.text: You come to a complete stop first.
You wait for the light to change.
You are in the correct lane and the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are in the correct lane and the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: If you are in a lane with a green arrow, you can go in that direction when the road is clear. This is true whether the arrow appears alone or with another signal.

questions.question: You must yield to a pedestrian:

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
Always, even if they are breaking traffic laws.
Only if the traffic light favors them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always, even if they are breaking traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Always watch for pedestrians near your car. Do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter the circumstances.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A crossroad is ahead.
Merge.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: A crossroad is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is coming ahead.

questions.question: On a multilane road, a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: No one can pass.
Everyone can pass.
Only the car next to the dashed line can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only the car next to the dashed line can pass.
questions.explanation: When one line is solid and one is dashed, only the driver next to the dashed line can cross and pass. The driver next to the solid line cannot pass.

questions.question: You cannot block an intersection during rush hour:

options.text: Unless you entered on a green light.
Ever, even if your light is green.
Unless you have the right-of-way or a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ever, even if your light is green.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can cross it completely before the light turns red, even if your light is green. You can get a ticket for blocking an intersection.

questions.question: If you see a stopped school bus with flashing lights and the signal arm out, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Go 15 mph if no children are visible.
Go normal speed but watch for children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: Always stop when you see a school bus with flashing lights and the arm extended. Stay stopped until the arm goes back and the bus moves. This rule applies whether you are going the same direction or coming from the other direction.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with no curb, turn your front wheels:

options.text: Left, toward the street.
Right, away from the street.
Straight, parallel with the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, away from the street.
questions.explanation: When parking on a hill (uphill or downhill) with no curb, turn your wheels so the car will roll away from the road if the brakes fail.

questions.question: You can get a speeding ticket for driving 55 mph in a 55 mph zone:

options.text: Never, because it is legal.
If road or weather conditions require slower driving.
Only if you are near a sharp curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: If road or weather conditions require slower driving.
questions.explanation: Never drive faster than is safe for the conditions. Even if you are under the speed limit, you can be ticketed if conditions require slower driving. Consider other traffic, road surface, pedestrians, and weather when choosing your speed.

questions.question: When making a right turn at a corner, what should you do?

options.text: You cannot enter the bicycle lane.
You can merge into the bicycle lane only if you stop before turning.
You must merge into the bicycle lane before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must merge into the bicycle lane before turning.
questions.explanation: When making a right turn where there is a bicycle lane, merge into it no more than 200 feet before the corner. Then make your turn. Check that no bicyclists are in your path before merging.

questions.question: Which child needs a child passenger restraint system?

options.text: A 9-year-old who is 4 feet 10 inches tall
A 10-year-old who is 5 feet 3 inches tall
A 7-year-old who is 4 feet 8 inches tall

questions.correctAnswerText: A 7-year-old who is 4 feet 8 inches tall
questions.explanation: Children who are 8 years old or older, or who are at least 4 feet 9 inches tall, can use a regular safety belt. All other children must use a child passenger restraint system.

questions.question: What do rumble strips do?

options.text: They warn drivers about tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They vibrate and make noise to alert tired or distracted drivers that they are leaving the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They vibrate and make noise to alert tired or distracted drivers that they are leaving the road.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips create noise and vibrations to warn drowsy or distracted drivers that they are drifting off the road or approaching a stop sign or signal.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?

options.text: Before you start driving.
Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before moving your vehicle. Also adjust your seat, fasten your safety belt, and secure items in and on your vehicle. Never adjust mirrors while driving.

questions.question: Can you cross a single broken white centerline?

options.text: No, you must stay in your lane.
Yes, you can cross it to change lanes.
Yes, but only from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, you can cross it to change lanes.
questions.explanation: White lines show lanes going the same direction. A broken white line means you can pass another vehicle when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Where should a driver look while driving?

options.text: Straight ahead at the road in front of the car.
Only at the middle of the road.
To the sides, ahead, and behind the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the sides, ahead, and behind the car.
questions.explanation: A good driver watches all around their vehicle. Know what is happening in all directions.

questions.question: Which statement about roadwork zones is true?

options.text: Fines in work zones are the same as fines on regular roads.
You must slow down for work zones.
Slow down only if you see workers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down for work zones.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop for road equipment. Driving carefully through work zones keeps drivers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and workers safe.

questions.question: What should you do before starting the engine?

options.text: Buckle your own safety belt.
Make sure all passengers buckle their safety belts.
Do both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do both of the above.
questions.explanation: Before starting the engine, buckle your safety belt and make sure all passengers do the same. Make this part of your routine.

questions.question: What rule helps prevent tailgating?

options.text: The one-second rule.
The two-second rule.
The three-second rule.

questions.correctAnswerText: The three-second rule.
questions.explanation: Most rear-end crashes are caused by tailgating. Use the three-second rule: when the car ahead passes a point, count "one-thousand-one, one-thousand-two, one-thousand-three." If you reach that point before you finish counting, you are too close.

questions.question: What do you do when a blind pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane crosses the street?

options.text: You must always let them cross.
You must tell them where to cross.
You only need to let them cross at corners.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always let them cross.
questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind people may use a guide dog or white cane. You must always yield to them, no matter where they are crossing.

questions.question: Which factor affects how fast a person absorbs alcohol?

options.text: Weight
Height
Intelligence

questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: Weight, biological sex, how much food is in the stomach, and how many drinks a person has had all affect alcohol absorption. Time is the only way to remove alcohol from the body.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow-moving vehicle.
Road construction or maintenance area.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: This sign is displayed on slow-moving vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do if there is a deep puddle ahead on the road?

options.text: Keep your speed to get through the water.
Avoid the puddle if possible.
Shift into neutral while driving through the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the puddle if possible.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like ice, wet leaves, oil, and deep puddles to prevent skidding. The safest surface to drive on is dry and solid.

questions.question: Where can you legally keep an open alcoholic drink in your car?

options.text: Under the front seat.
In the glove compartment.
In the trunk.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the trunk.
questions.explanation: Open alcoholic drinks must be stored in the trunk or a place where passengers do not sit. Never put an open drink in the glove compartment. This rule does not apply to passengers in buses, taxis, campers, or motor homes.

questions.question: What speed should you drive when entering a freeway?

options.text: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
At the legal speed limit.
Slower than freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Enter a freeway at or near the speed of traffic, unless traffic is going faster than the legal speed limit.
